we isolated a cDNA clone of the luciferin-regulated luciferase gene of the Japanese fire fly, Luciola crucita, and that the deduced primary structure of the protein is 548 amino acids with a molecular weight of 60024 and an isoelectric point of 5.2.
the Genji firefly (L. cruciata) luciferase cDNA was cloned from a cDNA expression library and that the primary structure of the enzyme was determined.

the amino acid sequences for Genji firefly Luciferase were cloned and analyzed, and that the primary structures of the Genji firefly and North American firely luciferases were found to be 67% homologous, with many changes found in the first part of the amino acid sequence.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the amino acid sequences around the active site of the Genji firefly are very different from those of the North American firefly.
the amino acid sequences in the first 150 aa of Genji fireflies are different from those of North American fireflies, and the difference is responsible for the difference in color.

the luciferin binding region is conserved between Genji and North-American firefly luciferins, and the amino acid residues responsible for the difference in light emission between the two fireflies are located at the N terminus and the carboxy terminal of the luciferases.
